- Large, irregular necrotic areas covering most of the leaf
- Dark brown/gray-brown coloration
- Some remaining green/yellow patches
- Water-soaked or collapsed texture
- No distinct concentric rings, white powder, or small spots

Top candidates: **Late Blight** (large irregular dark brown lesions, water-soaked) or **Gray Mold** (gray-brown necrosis).

Viewing one reference image for Late Blight:

The Late Blight reference shows a very similar pattern to the test image:
- Large, irregular dark brown/gray-brown necrotic areas
- Remaining green tissue at leaf margins
- Collapsed, water-soaked texture
- Same general distribution of lesion spread

The match is strong. Both images show the characteristic spreading necrosis of Late Blight (Phytophthora infestans) with the same brownish-gray coloration and irregular large lesions covering most of the leaf surface.
